headline: External biological knowledge encoded as structural priors in deep prediction models
label: Biological Priors In Prediction Models
summary: Recent preprints and Bioinformatics papers encode ontology, marker, and pathway knowledge as inductive structure in omics prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is external biological knowledge used as a constraint on learning rather than as a new architecture class. MSGR imposes a four-level Gene Ontology tree as a coarse-to-fine decoding scaffold for spatial expression prediction from histopathology images. BioExPL aligns neural network latent representations with curated genetic biomarker priors, and PRISM transfers scRNA-seq labels to spatial data via biological marker priors. Other items instead rely on co-expression-guided gene partitioning, frozen foundation-model features, or LLM-ranked neighbor drugs, so the shared pattern is not universal. What is new is encoding ontology, marker, and pathway knowledge as inductive structure within otherwise standard deep pipelines.
